This change returns a dictionary and callers now consume .values(), but the documented return contract still tells readers to expect a list; iterating the documented result as a list would instead yield group keys.
Docstring says 'returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult' but signature/body now return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Update docstring to describe dict keyed by group_key.

The evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. The method now returns a dict mapping group key to `DetectorEvaluationResult`. Update the docstring to describe the dict return shape.

issues.descricao: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
issues.textoGolden: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

comentarios.texto: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value: int` parameter but never uses it — the returned IssueOccurrence is derived only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Because `value` is dead, callers can pass a mismatched value with no failure: in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `6`. Either use `value` when constructing the occurrence so the test validates the group value, or drop the unused parameter and pass the correct value; otherwise the test silently accepts wrong group values.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Removing the cacheMu.Lock() that spanned the whole BuildIndex lets GetIndex (RLock) return nil while a build for the same key is still in flight. WHY: getOrCreateIndex (search.go:298) builds with the builder doing ListIterator over the entire resource (Limit 1000000000000); previously the RLock in GetIndex blocked until the concurrent build finished and cached the index, now every concurrent Search for the same un-indexed key starts its own full-resource build, duplicating heavy DB scans and creating duplicate bleve indexes. HOW: serialize builds per key (a per-key mutex / in-flight map) or keep the coarse lock so GetIndex blocks during a build; a global lock defeats the intended cross-namespace parallelism, so prefer a per-key guard.

WHAT: The new log line calls s.search.TotalDocs() while the event-watch goroutine started a few lines above can concurrently write b.cache in BuildIndex. WHY: TotalDocs (bleve.go:146) ranges over b.cache without holding cacheMu, so it races with the `b.cache[key] = idx` write under Lock, producing a fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' runtime error that crashes the process. HOW: have TotalDocs take b.cacheMu.RLock() (and skip entries whose type assertion is not *bleveIndex) so the map iteration is synchronized.

issues.descricao: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.
issues.textoGolden: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Removing the function-wide `b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()` and keeping only the lock around `b.cache[key]=idx` removes the only thing that serialized GetIndex against an in-flight build. WHY: getOrCreateIndex (resource/search.go:287-307) does GetIndex -> if nil -> build; previously BuildIndex held the write lock for its whole body so a concurrent caller's GetIndex (RLock) blocked until the first build cached the index and then saw it (no second build). Now GetIndex can return nil while a build for the same key is still running, so two requests/watch events build the SAME key concurrently — producing two distinct index instances where the caller holding the non-cached one never observes later writes (stale search results), and, for file-backed indices (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` opening the same on-disk directory. HOW: guard the build per key (e.g. re-check the cache under the write lock after acquiring it, or use a per-key single-flight/lock so only one build runs per NamespacedResource), rather than relying on a global write lock held for the entire body.

The cache mutex was moved to cover only the cache assignment, removing the serialization that previously surrounded the whole BuildIndex. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now both construct an index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk path) and both write `b.cache[key]`; the second overwrites the first, so callers get distinct index instances for one key and writes made through the losing instance are invisible to readers of the cached one (and the file-backed build may collide on the same directory). Keep the build for a given key serialized (e.g. restore the lock around the build, or take a per-key lock) instead of locking only the map write.

Locking only cache publication allows concurrent requests for the same uncached key to build separate indexes and overwrite each other's cache entries. Search and handleEvent both call getOrCreateIndex, whose GetIndex previously blocked behind the build-wide lock; now an event can update one newly built index before another build replaces it, losing that update from subsequent search results and leaving the discarded index open. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that per-key guard.

issues.descricao: The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
issues.textoGolden: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

comentarios.texto: The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call is unsafe: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-150) iterates `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`, while the bleve.go hunk in this same PR keeps `cacheMu` for the `b.cache[key] = idx` write only. Because search.go:207-213 already started the watch-event goroutine that can call `build` → `BuildIndex` → cache write, line 216 can iterate the map concurrently with that write, causing a `concurrent map iteration and map write` panic or data race. Either guard the `TotalDocs` read with `cacheMu`, or move this call to a point where no build can run concurrently.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs after launching the write-event listener, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu.RLock. A write event for an unindexed resource can concurrently publish an index through BuildIndex, causing a map iteration/write race and potentially a fatal runtime error during initialization. Protect TotalDocs cache iteration with the same read lock used by GetIndex.

BuildIndex now writes b.cache under Lock while TotalDocs (called from search.init after the watch goroutine starts) ranges over b.cache without any lock. This can cause a concurrent map read/write fatal error. Fix by taking cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

issues.descricao: NewResourceServer returns an error when Init fails without cancelling the server context created earlier.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and, on error, returns `nil, err` without invoking the `cancel` func created at line 229 and without running any lifecycle cleanup. WHY: Init may have already started long-lived goroutines — searchSupport.init's event-consumption loop uses context.Background() (resource/search.go:202) and initWatcher starts a watcher bound to s.ctx (server.go:752-770) — so if search.init succeeds and initWatcher (or a later step) fails, the constructor discards the server while those goroutines keep running with no way to stop them, leaking the internal context and watcher goroutines. HOW: on the error path call `cancel()` (and any needed lifecycle.Stop) before returning, or defer the cancel until success.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously but returns nil,err without calling the cancel created for s.ctx. WHY: Failed startup leaks the server context (and any lifecycle/watch resources partially started by Init), leaving goroutines/channel watches alive. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (and lifecycle Stop cleanup) before returning.

issues.descricao: The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: the align-items() mixin emits only -webkit-box-align as its legacy prefix while the flexbox() mixin it is paired with sets display:-moz-box for legacy Gecko. WHY: in an engine that selects display:-moz-box, no corresponding -moz-box-align is emitted, so the requested center/baseline alignment is dropped and the item stretches instead — the opposite of the author's intent and inconsistent with the declared 'all prefixes' goal. HOW: add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` alongside the existing -webkit-box-align declaration.

issues.descricao: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.

comentarios.texto: The flex-item styling targets the inner .extra-info-wrapper rather than the outer div generated by header-extra-info's Ember.Component. With .contents now using flexbox, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so a long nowrap topic title cannot shrink to the available space and pushes the navigation panel outside the header instead of being ellipsized by the existing desktop truncation rules. Move the extra-info-wrapper class onto the component's root element and set min-width: 0 on that flex item so ordering and truncation apply to the actual header child.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

comentarios.texto: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which never existed in IE/Edge; the legacy property is -ms-flex-align, so the declaration is dead.
issues.textoGolden: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: align-items() mixin emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is not a valid IE10/11 property (only -ms-flex-align exists). WHY: dead declaration shows wrong contract and leaves IE alignment dependent solely on -ms-flex-align, which also breaks for flex-start/flex-end values. HOW: remove the -ms-align-items line and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align.

issues.descricao: Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.
issues.textoGolden: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

issues.descricao: After .small-action becomes a flex container, float: left on .topic-avatar is dead CSS.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.
remove() always queries idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias), adding a database lookup on every IDP removal even when the cached entry already holds the model.
In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

issues.descricao: The caching tests for getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions were removed in the Prisma.sql conversion, leaving the cached-condition logic untested.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.

Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

issues.descricao: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so the hidden webauthn form is guaranteed by isPasskeysEnabled() and the new per-user isConfiguredFor check for users without a passkey is never exercised in UsernamePasswordForm.
